about: REE-265 step 0, every subject since REE-274: the ceilings of the work one answer may make, per state (tools/answercost.js; CI's "answer cost" job counts every state, tests/answercost.test.js holds the pure parts): fish, corals and sea slugs, each at 50, 500 and 3,000 answers, for a player in the middle of a session (the page's clock 30 s after the state's last answer), signed out. The players are made on a pinned version of the app (answercost.js PLAYERS_AT, a commit of main), so a later change of the draw does not change them. Each ceiling is the largest count measured over the page's seeds 1 to 3 (the same state and seed give counts that differ by up to 15% from run to run, the seeds by up to 50% on fish:3000), times the margin, rounded up to two significant digits, at least 100 calls. History: fish and corals at 50, 500 (fish) and 3,000 were set on main after #1522, tightened when the units in play became a view of the state version (REE-265 step 3: fn:bonusCalc in place of fn:bonusList) and when the tree's score and the levels did (step 4: fn:lvStepCalc in place of fn:lvStep; the storage read rose where views are read unit by unit); all nine states were set again, on the pinned players, when REE-274 added the sea slugs and the corals at 50 and 500 and moved the counts to CI. A step that lowers a count tightens its ceilings in the same PR: node tools/answercost.js --seed 1,2,3 --write-budget tools/answercost-budget.json --margin 1.25 (--states for the states it touches).
